title: Grateful Dead Live at West Palm Beach Auditorium on 1982-09-11
lineage: Cassettes > Sony TC-D5M > Audiophile 2496 Analog RCA Input > Soundforge > CD-Wave > TLH > FLAC
source: Two AUD cassette sources of unknown lineage

ai_review.summary: Audience recording of a high‑energy early‑80s show with standout Scarlet>Fire and soaring Garcia work, captured in decent sound quality.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its blazing Jerry Garcia solos – especially the Scarlet > Fire sequence, Sailor, Terrapin Station and a powerful Stella Blue – and a strong first set that includes Dupree’s, Loser and Let It Grow. Reviewers note the tape is an audience (AUD) source with acceptable clarity; no major mix problems are reported, though one listener mentions Phil’s bass is buried by his own speakers.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show highly (4‑5 stars) and highlight exceptional Garcia playing, while recording comments are generally neutral to positive; a few negative notes about song labeling keep confidence at medium.

recording_quality.technical_notes: No serious drop‑outs or muddiness reported; sound is clear enough for enjoyment, though one reviewer felt Phil’s bass was not prominent due to playback equipment rather than the tape itself.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A tight first set that builds momentum into a fiery second set; transitions such as Scarlet > Fire and Sailor > Saint are highlighted as especially effective.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia is described as ‘in overdrive’, delivering scorching solos on Scarlet>Fire, Sailor, Terrapin Station and ballads like Stella Blue; his vocals are praised despite early‑80s health concerns.
band_member_comments.Phil: One listener notes Phil’s bass isn’t loud enough, attributing this to the reviewer’s laptop speakers rather than performance quality.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir is said to work hard on lyrics but lacks emotional connection in his vocal delivery; still credited for keeping momentum with Around & Around.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (keyboards) receives strong praise for his contributions and chemistry with Jerry throughout the set.
